firstImpression: The pill reads 'Collaboration, Visibility, Flexibility' and the headline says 'Built for robust collaboration, smarter processes, and measurable outcomes' - that is the same generic workflow-tool language I have filed under 'another Asana' before, so I am scanning hard for my own words before I trust this.
comprehension: I would call this a compliant collaboration and automation layer, chat, forms, dashboards, e-signatures, that claims to sit under or beside FDA/ISO regulated work. It says the right nouns further down: 'Real-Time Audit Trail,' 'eSignatures (CFR Part 11 Compliant),' 'Revision Management / Version Control,' 'Cycle Time Tracking,' and a testimonial about 'management review.' But it never once says CAPA, deviation, or change order, it just says 'records' and 'processes.' And it never tells me if this replaces our QMS or plugs into it. The only place I see 'system of record' language at all is a boilerplate paragraph repeated under every single section, not in the actual feature copy, so I still cannot place this next to the QMS we already own.
resonanceReason: Anchor 2: interested with reservations. JTBD match is real and named: 'Cycle Time Tracking' matches our cycle-time hook, and the testimonial 'We used dashboards for management review. Instead of spending hours compiling data...' is close to word for word our management-review JTBD. 'Real-Time Audit Trail,' 'CFR Part 11 Compliant eSignatures,' and 'Revision Management / Version Control' hit our resonates vocabulary directly. Objections that block the next step: the page never names CAPA, deviation, or ECO, only generic 'records,' which is exactly the 'generic workflow-tool language that never names the QMS world' pattern our objections flag. It also never answers whether this replaces our QMS or sits next to it, the only 'system of record' language is buried in repeated boilerplate, not in the feature copy where I'd expect an answer. Both are named objections from the persona file, so this lands at 2, not 3.
